title: Autopsy and Confession
premise: Retired detective Vesper Oyelaran has spent a decade hiding behind the counter of their failing bookshop, the only family they trust being the ragtag regulars who drift through its doors. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after a stranger's funeral, naming Vesper as the only person who can undo a thirty-year-old murder, they are pulled back into a case whose alibis were woven by people who are now dying one by one. As Vesper unravels a conspiracy protected by the town's founding families, they realize the confessor is still alive, killing to keep the letter's promise from reaching anyone else. In the end, Vesper must choose between handing justice to courts that failed thirty years ago or letting the last conspirator fall to the vigilante they've come to understand—and in doing so, finally claim the found family that was waiting for them all along.
about_author: Ansel Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town coroner's assistant who spent fifteen years transcribing other people's final words before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet places where old sins refuse to stay buried, and live with two cats named after unsolved cases.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Vesper Oyelaran, POV. A confession letter arrives postmarked the day after a funeral for a man Vesper never met, confessing to a thirty-year-old murder and naming Vesper alone. The emotional beat is reluctant curiosity curdling into dread as Vesper recognizes the handwriting of someone they once arrested and lost.

chapters.title: The Regulars
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Vesper canvasses their bookshop regulars—an ex-con barista, a retired librarian, a teenage runaway—half to investigate, half because they're the closest thing to family Vesper has. One regular recognizes the victim's name from her own childhood. The beat is warmth shadowed by the realization that the past touches everyone in the room.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Digging into the 1994 case files, Vesper finds five witnesses whose alibis interlock too perfectly, each covering for the others. Two are already dead under ambiguous circumstances. The beat is cold satisfaction of detective work giving way to horror: the confessor is eliminating witnesses in order.

chapters.title: What the Librarian Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating: Vesper and Marisol the librarian. Marisol admits she was the sixth witness, hidden from the file because she was fourteen. She kept a photograph proving the timeline was staged. The beat is fragile trust—Vesper accepting help, Marisol risking exposure after decades of silence.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The third surviving witness dies hours before Vesper reaches him; the scene is staged as an accident but bears the confessor's signature detail from the original crime. Police dismiss Vesper as a meddlesome retiree. The beat is fury and guilt—the race was lost by exactly one afternoon.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Forensic comparison reveals the letter was written recently but signed with ink and paper from 1994—a message meant to be sent long ago, delayed by fear. Vesper realizes the confessor isn't taunting them; they're asking to be stopped. The beat is a shift from hunter to would-be rescuer.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The four original alibi-witnesses were the town's founding families' children; the victim was an outsider who saw something he shouldn't have. The fourth witness offers Vesper money to stop digging. The beat is vertigo—justice here was never merely delayed, it was purchased.

chapters.title: Where the Runaway Sleeps
chapters.summary: Alternating: Vesper and Theo the runaway. The confessor contacts Theo through the bookshop, believing the shop hides the last witness. Theo, terrified of losing the only place they belong, lies to protect everyone. The beat is found family tested—the shop itself becomes bait, and Veper must decide what it's worth.

chapters.title: The Last Alibi
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Climax at the drowned quarry where the original murder happened. Vesper confronts the confessor—the victim's sibling, who witnessed everything at nine years old and has spent thirty years executing the alibi list. The fourth witness arrives to finish the job. The beat is terrible recognition: Vesper holding both killers and the law equally powerless.

chapters.title: Autopsy and Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Resolution. Vesper chooses neither court nor quarry: they extract a full recorded confession implicating the founding families, then give the confessor a choice—surrender to the reopened case, or vanish with Vesper's silence. The bookshop reopens with a new sign reading 'open late.' The beat is hard-won belonging: justice outside the law, family inside the shop.
